messages:
kevin: Hey team — Acme demo next Wed. They want a 2-hour stress run that hits ~4x our normal QPS. Need a POC Dedicated pool bump and a short burst window. Can we do a temporary reservation + burst policy change?

anya: Yep. Do we want scheduled uplift (time window) or an on-demand burst token?

kevin: Scheduled preferred. Demo Wed 18:00–20:00 PST. Also they asked if this creates committed spend or just transient billing.

sam: If we add a short reservation (pre-warm + reserved for the window) it counts as reserved capacity for the duration. Burst mode would be pay-as-you-go but can queue if other tenants use GPUs.

jess: For POCs we usually do a hybrid: small reservation (1–2 GPUs) + burst policy to cover spikes. Minimizes cost while keeping latency SLOs.

kevin: Their workload estimate: ~600 reqs/min at peak, short prompts. Propose numbers?

sam: With our worker profile, 1 A10-equiv handles ~150 reqs/min at that prompt shape. So reserve 4 workers to hit 600, plus 2 workers headroom = burst_limit 6.

anya: Drafting pool change. Two options:
- Option A: reservation=4, burst_limit=6, window 2026-03-25T18:00:00-08:00 to 2026-03-25T20:00:00-08:00 (2h)
- Option B: reservation=2, burst_limit=8, same window (cheaper reserved cost, more pay-as-you-go risk)

kevin: They want predictable latency → Option A. Also asked about ephemeral API keys scoped to the pool for the POC.

jess: We can issue an ephemeral hosted API key scoped to the Dedicated pool for the window; it will expire after the window. For security questionnaire: need VPC peering and ATO checklist.

kevin: They flagged network isolation — want VPC peering for log egress. Will peering affect pool resizing?

sam: Peering is separate but must be ready before we issue ephemeral keys. It doesn’t block resizing, but we should avoid key issuance until firewall rules are confirmed. Peering usually takes 24–48h.

anya: Action items:
- sam: create reservation change request for pool "poc-acme-nyc" with reservation=4, burst_limit=6, window Wed 18:00–20:00 PST.
- jess: generate ephemeral API key and scope once VPC peering confirmed.
- anya: update pricing estimate and send to Acme for signoff.

sam: Opening infra ticket now. Config to apply:
{ "pool_id": "poc-acme-nyc", "reservation_workers": 4, "burst_max_workers": 6, "scaling_window": { "start": "2026-03-25T18:00:00-08:00", "end": "2026-03-25T20:00:00-08:00" }, "prewarm": true }

sam: Note: prewarm=true provisions containers ~10 minutes before start. If we need extra safety, extend to 30 minutes.

kevin: 10 minutes OK. Also add an autoscale fallback to a cheaper quantized model if workers saturate — Acme wants cost controls.

jess: Set fallback: if queue latency > 250ms for 30s, route to model x-small-quant. Document in demo runbook so they’re aware of potential quality drop.

anya: Pricing estimate: reservation 4 workers for 2h + expected burst -> ~$420 reservation + up to $180 burst worst-case. Sending quote to Acme.

kevin: Confirm when infra ticket is live and ephemeral key ready.

sam: Infra ticket created: INF-2026-789. Scheduled change window set, waiting infra approval on VPC peering. ETA for resize: 2026-03-24 22:00 UTC (to complete before demo).

deploy-bot: Pool change scheduled: poc-acme-nyc resize job queued (job id 8844). Start: 2026-03-25T17:50:00-08:00.

jess: Holding ephemeral key until deploy-bot confirms pool ready and VPC peering is green.

kevin: Great — I’ll notify Acme and ask them to confirm security side. :thumbsup: 

anya: TL;DR: Option A (reservation=4, burst_limit=6) approved by sales. Tickets: INF-2026-789; deploy job 8844. Next: confirm VPC peering + issue ephemeral key.

kevin: Closing loop — thanks all!
